record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How many words of a given length are strongly k-abelian nth powers?

evidence.quote: How many words of a given length are strongly k- abelian nth powers? Author: Michaël Rao [40, 39–46]. Given an integern>= 2, a word u is a k-abelian-n-power if we haveu = u1u2··· un, where ui and ui+1 are k-abelian equivalents for every iin{ 1,··· n- 1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and an integer $k\geq 1$. Two finite words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u\sim_k v$, if for every word $w\in\Sigma^*$ with $|w|\leq k$, the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $w$ as a factor of $v$. For an integer $n\geq 2$, a word $W\in\Sigma^*$ is called a strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th power if it can be written as a concatenation $W=u_1u_2\cdots u_n$ where $u_i\sim_k u_{i+1}$ for every $i\in\{1,2,\ldots,n-1\}$ (so all blocks $u_i$ have the same length and are pairwise $k$-abelian equivalent to consecutive blocks).

Determine, as a function of the length $N$ (and of the parameters $k$, $n$, and $|\Sigma|$), the number of words in $\Sigma^N$ that are strongly $k$-abelian $n$-th powers. Equivalently, give an exact formula or asymptotic expression for $|\{W\in\Sigma^N : W\text{ is a strongly }k\text{-abelian }n\text{-th power}\}|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The enumeration of strongly k-abelian n-th powers is mentioned as an open problem in the combinatorics-on-words literature. Existing results (e.g., Karhumäki et al.) address unavoidability and growth of k-abelian equivalence classes, but no explicit formula or asymptotic count for the number of length-N words that are strongly k-abelian n-th powers appears in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Strongly k-abelian nth powers are not avoidable on any alphabet for any numbers k and n.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work addresses unavoidability of strongly k-abelian n-th powers but not their exact enumeration.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Combinatorics on Words: a Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of abelian/k-abelian combinatorics on words including powers and equivalence classes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys do not report a closed-form count of strongly k-abelian n-th powers of given length.

status_evidence.title: k-Abelian Equivalence and Factor Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: The number of k-abelian equivalence classes of words of length n grows polynomially.
status_evidence.claim: Counting k-abelian classes is studied, but counting strongly k-abelian n-th powers is not resolved.
